The passage from the Rig Veda describes the divine, cosmological origins of the four main varnas (Brahman, Kshatriya, Vaishya, Shudra) through the sacrifice of the primordial being Purusa. This frames the caste system as having a religious and cosmic basis, not merely a social or political one.  

Option (A) is contradicted by the text, since it presents the caste system as divinely ordained, not a social construct of its time.  
Option (B) is not supported — there’s no mention of regional princes or political motives.  
Option (C) is irrelevant to the passage, which predates Muslim invasions by over two millennia.  
Option (D) fits best, because the text shows the caste system as part of Hindu religious tradition from ancient times, transcending specific historical periods.  

Final answer: (D)
